text:
anna: quick thread — we need to tweak the loadgen to reproduce microbursts + long-tail KV cache effects that triggered the kernel-selection perf regression. current ramp generator smooths too much; tails don't match prod.

rahul: agree. can you sketch the traffic envelope you want? p95 vs p99 shape?

anna: sketch: 3-phase run (cold -> warm -> hot) for KV warmup. during hot phase inject microbursts (3-10k qps spikes lasting 200-800ms) with randomized gaps. overlay a long-tail background (pareto inter-arrival, alpha ~1.2) to simulate sporadic big requests. goal: make batching heuristics see both high-concurrency and very sparse windows.

liz: +1. For apples-to-apples comparisons: run against identical model binary and kernel set, use fixed seq-len=256 baseline and variable-seq experiment. record per-step kernel choice and batch occupancy histograms.

mike: how do we encode the microburst envelope in loadgen? share a config snippet pls.

anna: paste config draft:
```
# phases: 60s cold, 300s warm, 120s hot
phases:
  - name: cold
    duration_s: 60
    target_qps: 200
  - name: warm
    duration_s: 300
    target_qps: 800
  - name: hot
    duration_s: 120
    base_qps: 800
    microbursts:
      rate_per_min: 6
      spike_qps: [6000, 10000]
      spike_duration_ms: [200, 800]
      inter_burst_dist: pareto(alpha=1.5)
background:
  long_tail:
    distribution: pareto
    alpha: 1.2
    scale: 1
kv_warmup:
  hot_key_fraction: 0.02
  prefill_duration_s: 30
record:
  metrics: [p50, p95, p99, p999, throughput, avg_batch_size, kernel_tags]
  sampling_ms: 100
```

sara: also log KV cache hit-rate over time and per-key access. inject hot-key skew with zipf s=1.1. we noticed regressions only when hit-rate dipped below ~70%.

rahul: for kernel-selection comparisons: run two variants back-to-back with the same arrival randomness. add `--replay-seed=42` so the arrival stream is identical. pin NUMA, cgroups, and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to avoid noisy pages.

liz: add perf counters: GPU utilization, kernel runtime breakdown, memcpy times, stall cycles. tag runs with `perf-agent` and include timestamps so we can correlate batch sizes with kernel choice.

mike: ci-bot: can you queue a quick smoke run with this config on staging?

ci-bot: queued: loadgen/1795001123/kv-microburst-v1 — will run on staging/gpu-pool-2, notify when done.

sara: we'll need to aggregate batch-occupancy histograms across runs to compute cost-per-token tradeoffs. recommend weighted CDFs and heatmaps (batch-size vs latency).

anna: next steps: I'll open a small PR with the loadgen microburst patch and prefill script. baseline run on staging today, then run smart-batching heuristic enabled in variant B. if we reproduce the regression, file perf bug with kernel tags + trace.

rahul: i'll add instrumentation for kernel tags and batch histos; aim EOD.

liz: one minor note — make KV warmup deterministic: prefill hot keys from `prefill_keys.json` so hot-key set is stable across repeats.

mike: ack, i'll update the run wrapper to mount `prefill_keys.json` and set `--replay-seed`.

sara: also plan an A/B with quantized-kernel vs fallback (unquantized) to isolate whether quantization path is causing the tail.

anna: :thumbsup: thanks all. i'll post the PR link here once created.

ci-bot: run started: https://ci.internal.redwood/loadgen/1795001123/kv-microburst-v1

mike: great, tagging me when results land.

anna: if anyone sees weird noise, add `--log-samples=1` to capture exact request payloads for stray outliers.

liz: will do.

sara: thanks — excited to see if this reproduces the kernel fallback spike.
